title: Why This Trader Got a $1.3 Million Bonus
description:
Book a call with us so we can help you break into finance (investment banking, hedge funds, venture capital, private equity jobs and more): https://haroun.short.gy/finance-book-yt-o

Why would a trader receive a $1.3 million bonus?

In this scene from Billions, Bobby Axelrod breaks down one of the most important concepts in finance: the hedge fund compensation model known as "2 and 20."

A hedge fund typically charges a 2% annual management fee plus 20% of profits generated for investors. When you're managing billions of dollars, those numbers become massive very quickly.

In this breakdown, we calculate how a $10 billion hedge fund can generate hundreds of millions in fees and potentially billions in profit-sharing, creating enormous bonus pools for employees.

This clip provides a simple explanation of hedge fund economics, trader compensation, incentive structures, and why top finance professionals can earn extraordinary bonuses.

#Billions #HedgeFund #Investing #Finance #WallStreet

top_comments.author: @davidoconnor1773
top_comments.text: Hilariously outdated and incorrect video. 2 and 20 is barely used by hedge funds anymore, and a fund the size of Axe would not be using it. And funds don’t get performance fees based on profits, they get it on the delta that the fund performance exceeds the hurdle rate (say the fund hurdle rate tracks to an 8% benchmark for the S&P, and the fund returns 12% for the year, they’ve exceeded the hurdle by 4%, so it would be 20% of 4%, not 20% of 12%)
